nodes.title: Riemann Hypothesis
nodes.gist: Every non-trivial zero of the Riemann zeta function has real part exactly 1/2.
nodes.detail: Stated with Mathlib's own definition of RiemannHypothesis, so the target is the standard statement. In Main.lean it is a one-line alias of rhOfAll.

gb.note: Would not change the Goldbach-gap search: it controls where primes exist, not where they are absent.

nodes.source: theorem riemannHypothesis : RiemannHypothesis := rhOfAll

nodes.title: Zeta zeros on the line (archive wording)
nodes.gist: The same statement as the Riemann Hypothesis, written with the archive's own definition RiemannZetaZerosOnLine.
nodes.detail: Proved by the same theorem as the Riemann Hypothesis, so the two stand or fall together.
nodes.source: theorem riemannZeta_eq_zero_re : RiemannZetaZerosOnLine := rhOfAll

nodes.title: L-functions have no zeros right of 1/2
nodes.gist: For every Dirichlet character and every s with real part above 1/2, the L-function is not zero (the pole at s = 1 for the trivial character is excluded).
nodes.detail: This is the one-sided form of the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis. It is the statement the whole archive is built to prove; the other four claims follow from it by the functional equation.
nodes.source: theorem LFunction_ne_zero_of_half_lt_re : DirichletLNonvanishingRightOfHalf := allChi

nodes.title: All L-function zeros lie on the line
nodes.gist: Every zero of a Dirichlet L-function inside the critical strip has real part exactly 1/2.
nodes.detail: The two-sided Generalized Riemann Hypothesis for Dirichlet L-functions, taken from a bundle of three claims.
nodes.source: theorem LFunction_eq_zero_re : DirichletLZerosOnLine := claimAll.2.1

nodes.title: Primitive L-function zeros on the line
nodes.gist: The same two-sided statement, for primitive characters, using Mathlib's L-function.
nodes.detail: Proved by the critical-line theorem critAll.
nodes.source: theorem LFunction_eq_zero_re_of_isPrimitive : PrimitiveDirichletLZerosOnLine := critAll

nodes.title: RH from the key statement
nodes.gist: Applies the bridge theorem that turns the key statement (no zeros right of 1/2) into the Riemann Hypothesis.
nodes.detail: rhOfAll : RiemannHypothesis := rh_of_every allChi. Lives in Supplements.Kernels.MainTheorems.
nodes.source: theorem rhOfAll : RiemannHypothesis := Formalism.VW.rh_of_every allChi

nodes.title: The key statement, proved
nodes.gist: Names the proved fact 'L(s, chi) is nonzero for Re s > 1/2, for every character' so the three assembly theorems can reuse it.
nodes.detail: allChi is a one-line alias of UpperTheory.FinalTheorems.everyCharacter. This is where the assembly layer hands over to the real argument.
nodes.source: theorem allChi : UpperTheory.EveryCharacter := UpperTheory.FinalTheorems.everyCharacter

nodes.title: Critical line from the key statement
nodes.gist: Applies the bridge theorem that turns the key statement into 'all zeros of primitive L-functions lie on the line'.
nodes.source:
theorem critAll (N : ℕ) [NeZero N] (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ N) (hχ : χ.IsPrimitive) (s : ℂ)
    (h0 : 0 < s.re) (h1 : s.re < 1) (hz : LFunction χ s = 0) : s.re = 1 / 2 :=
  Formalism.VW.critLine allChi N χ hχ s h0 h1 hz

nodes.title: Bundle of the three claims
nodes.gist: Packages the half-plane statement, the strip statement and the zeta statement into one triple.
nodes.detail: claimAll := (allChi, Claim.strip allChi, Claim.zeta allChi).
nodes.source:
theorem claimAll : Claim.HalfPlane ∧ Claim.Strip ∧ Claim.Zeta :=
  ⟨allChi, Claim.strip allChi, Claim.zeta allChi⟩

nodes.title: Key statement => RH
nodes.gist: Takes the key statement for the trivial character modulo 1, whose L-function is the zeta function, and feeds it to the zeta-only version.
nodes.detail: Three lines of Lean. The trivial character mod 1 has L-function equal to the Riemann zeta function.
nodes.source:
theorem Formalism.VW.rh_of_every (h : UpperTheory.EveryCharacter) : RiemannHypothesis :=
  Formalism.VW.rh_of_right fun s hs hs1 => by
    have := h 1 (1 : DirichletCharacter ℂ 1) s hs (Or.inr hs1)
    rwa [LFunction_modOne_eq] at this

nodes.title: Zeta nonzero right of 1/2 => RH
nodes.gist: If zeta has no zeros with real part above 1/2, it has none below 1/2 either, so every non-trivial zero sits on the line.
nodes.detail: Proof by cases on whether Re s is below, equal to, or above 1/2. A zero below 1/2 is reflected to a zero above 1/2 by the functional equation, which is a contradiction.
nodes.source:
theorem Formalism.VW.rh_of_right (hz : ∀ s : ℂ, 1 / 2 < s.re → s ≠ 1 → riemannZeta s ≠ 0) : RiemannHypothesis := by
  unfold RiemannHypothesis
  intro s hs htriv hs1
  rcases lt_trichotomy s.re (1 / 2) with hlt | heq | hgt
  · exfalso
    have hpi : (Real.pi : ℂ) ≠ 0 := by exact_mod_cast Real.pi_ne_zero
    have hs0 : s ≠ 0 := by
      rintro rfl
      rw [riemannZeta_zero] at hs
      norm_num at hs
    have ht : 1 / 2 < (1 - s).re := by
      rw [Complex.sub_re, Complex.one_re]
      linarith
    have h1 : (1 - s) ≠ 1 := by
      intro h
      apply hs0
      linear_combination -h
    have hnat : ∀ n : ℕ, (1 - s) ≠ -(n : ℂ) := by
      intro n h
      have hr := congrArg Complex.re h
      rw [Complex.sub_re, Complex.one_re, Complex.neg_re, Complex.natCast_re] at hr
      have : (0 : ℝ) ≤ n := n.cast_nonneg
      linarith
    have key := riemannZeta_one_sub hnat h1
    rw [sub_sub_canc

nodes.title: Key statement => zeros on the line
nodes.gist: For a primitive character, a zero left of 1/2 would produce a zero of the conjugate character right of 1/2, which the key statement forbids.
nodes.detail: Uses the functional equation of the completed L-function and the fact that the Gamma factor does not vanish.
nodes.source:
theorem Formalism.VW.critLine (h : UpperTheory.EveryCharacter) (N : ℕ) [NeZero N] (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ N) (hχ : χ.IsPrimitive) (s : ℂ)
    (h0 : 0 < s.re) (h1 : s.re < 1) (hz : LFunction χ s = 0) : s.re = 1 / 2 := by
  have hs0 : s ≠ 0 := fun e => by simp [e] at h0
  have hs1 : s ≠ 1 := fun e => by simp [e] at h1
  by_contra hne
  rcases lt_or_gt_of_ne hne with hlt | hgt
  · have hinv : χ⁻¹.IsPrimitive := by
      rw [isPrimitive_def, conductor_inv]; exact hχ
    have hc : completedLFunction χ s = 0 := by
      rw [LFunction_eq_completed_div_gammaFactor χ s (Or.inl hs0)] at hz
      exact (div_eq_zero_iff.1 hz).resolve_right (Formalism.VW.gammaFactor_ne_zero χ h0)
    have hfe := hinv.completedLFunction_one_sub s
    rw [inv_inv, hc, mul_zero] at hfe
    have h2 : (1 - s) ≠ 0 := sub_ne_zero.2 hs1.symm
    refine h N χ⁻¹ (1 - s) (by rw [sub_re, one_re]; linarith) (Or.inr fun e => hs0
...

nodes.title: Gamma factor never vanishes
nodes.gist: For Re s > 0 the Gamma factor in the functional equation is nonzero, so zeros of an L-function and of its completed version coincide.
nodes.source:
theorem Formalism.VW.gammaFactor_ne_zero {N : ℕ} (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ N) {s : ℂ} (hs : 0 < s.re) : gammaFactor χ s ≠ 0 := by
  rcases χ.even_or_odd with h | h
  · rw [h.gammaFactor_def]; exact Gammaℝ_ne_zero_of_re_pos hs
  · rw [h.gammaFactor_def]; exact Gammaℝ_ne_zero_of_re_pos (by rw [add_re, one_re]; linarith)

nodes.title: Strip claim from half-plane
nodes.gist: Turns 'no zeros right of 1/2' into 'every zero in the critical strip has real part 1/2', by the same reflection argument.
nodes.detail: Case split on Re s < 1/2, = 1/2, > 1/2.
nodes.source:
theorem strip (h : HalfPlane) : Strip := by
  unfold HalfPlane at h
  intro N _ χ s hs0 hs1 hz
  have hs : s ≠ 1 := fun e => by rw [e, Complex.one_re] at hs1; exact lt_irrefl _ hs1
  have hs0' : s ≠ 0 := fun e => by rw [e, Complex.zero_re] at hs0; exact lt_irrefl _ hs0
  rcases lt_trichotomy s.re (1 / 2) with hlt | heq | hgt
  · exfalso
    haveI : NeZero χ.conductor := ⟨χ.conductor_ne_zero⟩
    have hp := prim_zero χ hs0 hs1 hz
    have hr := prim_reflect χ.primitiveCharacter χ.primitiveCharacter_isPrimitive hs0 hs1 hp
    have ht : (1 : ℂ) - s ≠ 1 := fun e => hs0' (sub_eq_self.mp e)
    exact h χ.conductor χ.primitiveCharacter⁻¹ (1 - s)
      (by rw [Complex.sub_re, Complex.one_re]; linarith) (Or.inr ht) hr
  · exact heq
  · exact absurd hz (h N χ s hgt (Or.inr hs))

nodes.title: Zeta claim from half-plane
nodes.gist: The zeta version of the strip claim, obtained from the trivial character modulo 1.
nodes.source:
theorem zeta (h : HalfPlane) : Zeta := by
  intro s hz htriv hs1
  have hs0 : s ≠ 0 := fun e => by rw [e, riemannZeta_zero] at hz; norm_num at hz
  rcases lt_or_ge 0 s.re with hpos | hnpos
  · rcases lt_or_ge s.re 1 with hlt1 | hge1
    · have hL : DirichletCharacter.LFunction (1 : DirichletCharacter ℂ 1) s = 0 := by
        rw [DirichletCharacter.LFunction_modOne_eq]; exact hz
      exact strip h 1 1 s hpos hlt1 hL
    · exact absurd hz (riemannZeta_ne_zero_of_one_le_re hge1)
  · exfalso
    have hG : Gammaℝ s ≠ 0 := by
      intro hg
      obtain ⟨n, hn⟩ := Complex.Gammaℝ_eq_zero_iff.mp hg
      rcases n with _ | n
      · exact hs0 (by simpa using hn)
      · exact htriv ⟨n, by rw [hn]; push_cast; ring⟩
    have hc : completedRiemannZeta s = 0 := by
      rw [riemannZeta_def_of_ne_zero hs0, div_eq_zero_iff] at hz
      exact hz.resolve_right hG
    have h1s : 1 - s ≠ 0 := fun e => by

nodes.title: Green + window => key theorem
nodes.gist: Green's classification of cuspidal characters over finite fields plus the window estimate gives zero-freeness for primitive characters; one more step extends it to all characters.
nodes.detail: Green says: for each prime g and degree d, cuspidal characters of GL_d over F_g are indexed by prime labels and have degree prod(g^i - 1). Combined with the window estimate it yields ZeroFreeAll.
nodes.source:
theorem UpperTheory.Top.every_character_of_green_v_win (hG : GlobalTheory.GLq.Green) (hV : UpperTheory.Top.VWin)
    (h : Nonempty (_root_.GlobalTheory.Fc.HypsAlt (fun 𝒞 => Closed 𝒞 fun Fm _ => LinkN Fm) _root_.GlobalTheory.Fc.DefiniteSideCondition)) : UpperTheory.EveryCharacter :=
  UpperTheory.Top.imprimitive (_root_.UpperTheory.Top.zero_free_all_of_green_v_win hG hV h)

nodes.title: Primitive => all characters
nodes.gist: An imprimitive character's L-function differs from its primitive version only by finitely many Euler factors, so zero-freeness passes from primitive characters to all characters.
nodes.detail: Proof goes through the primitive character associated to chi, with a special case for s = 1.
nodes.source:

    rcases hχs with hχ | hs1
    · left

  rw [χ.changeLevel_primitiveCharacter] at hrw
  rw [hrw]
  refine mul_ne_zero hL (Finset.prod_ne_zero_iff.mpr fun p hp => ?_)
  have hp' := Nat.prime_of_mem_primeFactors hp

nodes.title: Local Langlands for GL_n exists
nodes.gist: For every number field and every finite place there is a map from irreducible representations of GL_n over the local field to Weil-Deligne representations, satisfying the expected laws.
nodes.detail: RecTExists. Its proof builds Artin and cuspidal cases first, then extends by the Langlands classification (exists_isLExt). The main theorem needs it on several routes.
nodes.source:
theorem UpperTheory.Zero.LLC.recTExists :
    UpperTheory.Zero.LLC.RecTExists := by
  intro E Ω _ _ _ _ _ A w h
  obtain ⟨a, ha, -⟩ := UpperTheory.Zero.LLC.artEx E Ω A w h
  obtain ⟨r, hr⟩ := UpperTheory.Zero.LLC.cuspEx E Ω A w h a ha
  obtain ⟨⟨rc, hrc⟩, hcu⟩ :=
    GlobalTheory.LocLanglands.exists_isLExt UpperTheory.Zero.LLC.Pr.exh UpperTheory.Zero.LLC.Pr.multi E Ω A w h r
  have hcusp : ∀ x : IrrGL (HeightOneSpectrum.adicCompletion E w), x.IsCusp → rc x = r x :=
    hcu rc hrc
  have hD := UpperTheory.Zero.LLC.extDim E Ω A w h a ha r rc hr hrc
  have hT := UpperTheory.Zero.LLC.extTw E Ω A w h a ha r rc hr hrc
  refine ⟨rc, a, ha, ?_⟩
  refine
    { dim := fun x => (hD x).1.1
      one := fun χ hχ => (hcusp _ (IrrGL.isCusp_ofChar χ hχ)).trans (hr.one χ hχ)
      langlands := ?_
      cusp := ?_
      nu := hT.1
      absCentral := fun x ω hω σ => ((hD x).2 ω hω σ).1
      twist := ?_

nodes.title: Complex-multiplication toolkit
nodes.gist: Collects eight classical facts about abelian varieties with complex multiplication: deformation, de Rham, dual crystals, period comparison, Gauss-Manin, Serre-Tate, the main theorem of CM, and the Hilbert class field.
nodes.detail: Each field is proved by a separate theorem; two of them appear as nodes on this map.
nodes.source:
theorem UpperTheory.One.Join.cm_abelian_inputs_from_literature (O : _root_.UpperTheory.LiteratureTheorems.OpenImageCondition) : _root_.GlobalTheory.Mem.LiteralAutomorphy.LiteratureCMHypothesis where

nodes.gist: The least prime in any coprime residue class modulo q is at most C times q^L, for some constants C and L.
nodes.detail: The statement is existential, so no numeric exponent is available. Its Lean closure is 517 modules, the same set the Lean session built.

gb.note: Reusable and already built by the Lean session (517 files, about 1.4 core-hours). Used in Effective.lean.

  refine GlobalTheory.Published.linnik_iff_exists_prime.2 ⟨3, A, by norm_num, by linarith, fun a q _ hq hc => ?_⟩
  have hq1 : (1 : ℝ) ≤ (q : ℝ) ^ A := Real.one_le_rpow (by exact_mod_cast hq) (by linarith)
  by_cases h2 : 2 < q
  · obtain ⟨p, h1, h3, h4⟩ := h a q h2 hc
    exact ⟨p, h1, h3, by linarith⟩
  · refine ⟨3, Nat.prime_three, ?_, by push_cast; linarith⟩
    have : q = 1 ∨ q = 2 := by omega
    rcases this with rfl | rfl
    · exact Nat.modEq_one
    · have : a % 2 = 1 := Nat.odd_iff.1 (Nat.coprime_two_right.1 hc)
      unfold Nat.ModEq; omega

nodes.gist: If a set of integers in an interval of length N misses one residue class modulo every prime up to Q, its size is at most (Q^2 + 2 pi N) / ((phi(q)/q) log Q).

gb.note: Closure 106 files. For our covering instance the bound is 318,514 against a universe of 11,474 primes, so it says nothing there, and it bounds from above, not below.

edges.why: The zeta claim is the strip claim for the trivial character, so the same reflection argument is reused.
To pass between an L-function and its completed version across the functional equation, the Gamma factor must not vanish; otherwise a zero could appear or disappear in the reflection.
Specialising to the trivial character modulo 1 gives exactly the hypothesis the zeta-only theorem needs, because that character's L-function is zeta.
The no-zeros-right-of-1/2 claim is allChi itself. It is the one statement the archive actually has to prove; every other claim is derived from it.
The primitive-character version is the critical-line theorem applied to the key statement.
Main.lean defines the headline theorem as rhOfAll, so RH is exactly the key statement run through the zeta specialisation. Nothing else is added.
The two-sided statement for all Dirichlet L-functions is read off the bundle claimAll, which pairs the key statement with the strip and zeta claims.
The archive's own wording of RH is closed by the same theorem, so the two claims cannot come apart.
One of the eight CM facts: the Galois action on CM elliptic curves.
One of the eight CM facts: the Hilbert class field is generated by a j-invariant.
The covolume bound ends in an Arakelov good-tower volume theorem.
Packs its four inputs into the hypothesis 'literal automorphy at rank n' and applies the next theorem.
The Galois statement is proved by constructing the representations from a theta lift.
The construction takes the theta-lift property as an input.
The construction also takes a geometric realisation statement for weight-one forms.
Local-global compatibility of the constructed representations is stated in terms of local Langlands parameters, so the construction ends up using their existence.
The route through patching and Galois representations uses local Langlands existence, here through a chain of five references.
Base change for definite unitary groups is one of the six fields, supplied through a short wrapper.
Green's series statement is one of the six fields of the first batch.
Linnik's theorem is one of the six fields, supplied through a two-step wrapper.
To feed the zero-free argument it needs window prime pairs for each character, which this theorem constructs.
Uses the relative-error form of primes in progressions to control sums over the window primes.
A long chain of bounds on psi ends in Siegel-Walfisz; this is the only place on the map where a classical zero-free-region result is consumed.
Base change from definite unitary groups to GL_n is one of the three inputs of the window theorem.
The window estimate comes from a general theorem that combines open image, base change and the Galois statement.
The CM package (deformation, de Rham, Serre-Tate, main theorem of CM, class field) is passed in as the fourth input.
The window theorem is a thin wrapper over the depth-zero base-change-and-CM theorem.
allChi is a one-line alias. This is the hand-over from the assembly layer to the actual argument, so every claim in the archive rests on the single theorem everyCharacter.
Builds the strip claim from the key statement.
Builds the zeta claim from the key statement.
The first slot of the bundle is the key statement itself.
critAll calls the bridge theorem that moves zeros from left of 1/2 to right of 1/2.
Same input as RH: the key statement for all characters.
rhOfAll only calls the bridge theorem that converts the key statement into RH.
The bridge needs the key statement as its input; this is where the proof of RH becomes a proof of the key statement.
Linnik's theorem is proved from the relative-error estimate for primes in progressions. This is the first link in the analytic engine.
